collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A respected healer gave the wrong herb and made a patient worse: admit it publicly, or quietly change the practice.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject), the village's most respected healer, gave (friend) a bitter root for a stomach ache, mixed up with a different root. (friend) was sick for three days. (friend) is better now. (subject) is shaken. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) tells the gathering what happened and how (subject.he/she) will make sure it never happens again: roots kept apart, labeled with carved sticks. Some people trust (subject.him/her) less. More people trust (subject.him/her) more. (friend) says it took courage.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) apologizes to (friend) privately and quietly reorganizes the healing hut. Nobody else knows. (friend) is satisfied. (subject) still wakes at night thinking about it.
